item.text:
**Bottom Line**
Mixed, leaning negative. Jokowi’s 2024 record included real pro-investment and property-rights moves, especially land registration and a few market-opening steps. But the broader rule environment still looked restrictive on competition, trade, and business entry, with persistent regulatory barriers and market-power problems.

**Accepted Claims**

- **Indonesia’s Climate Ambitions Gain Boost through World Bank-Supported Land Administration and Spatial Planning Reform** — World Bank, 2024-09-30, [link](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/09/30/indonesia-s-climate-ambitions-gain-boost-through-world-bank-supported-land-administration-and-spatial-planning-reform)  
  The World Bank said the project was meant to strengthen land tenure security for millions of landholders, simplify business licensing, improve spatial planning, and reduce disputes and more productive investment. This is strong positive evidence for property rights and the investment climate.  
  IDs: `5B.4`, also `5B.1`

- **Indonesia, Japan agree on trade pact amendments to reduce barriers** — Reuters, 2024-08-08, [link](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/indonesia-japan-agree-on-trade-pact-amendments-to-reduce-barriers-3561549)  
  Indonesia and Japan agreed to amend their trade pact to reduce or remove trade barriers, cut tariffs on Indonesian products, and improve market access on both sides. This is positive evidence for trade openness and rules that support business activity.  
  IDs: `5B.4`

- **Indonesia launches 'Golden Visa' to lure foreign investors, boost economy** — Reuters, 2024-07-25, [link](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/indonesia-launches-golden-visa-to-lure-foreign-investors-boost-economy-3535351)  
  Jokowi launched a long-term visa scheme explicitly to attract foreign investors and boost the economy. That is positive evidence for investment conditions and a more welcoming framework for entrepreneurship and capital formation.  
  IDs: `5B.4`, also `5B.1`

- **Indonesia Economy Projected to Remain Resilient** — World Bank, 2024-06-24, [link](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/06/24/indonesia-economy-projected-to-remain-resilient)  
  The World Bank said Indonesia’s robust macroeconomic framework helped attract investment and that continued prudent, credible, transparent policy was needed to sustain growth. This supports a positive reading on investment conditions and the basic policy environment for firms.  
  IDs: `5B.4`, also `5B.3`

- **OECD Economic Surveys: Indonesia 2024** — OECD, 2024-11-26, [link](https://www.oecd.org/en/publications/oecd-economic-surveys-indonesia-2024_de87555a-en/full-report/accelerating-growth-and-attaining-socioeconomic-convergence_02e70f46.html)  
  The OECD said Indonesia remained relatively restrictive for business: price controls still existed, public procurement still had hurdles, foreign participation in tenders faced considerable barriers, administrative requirements for new firms were still high, and several FDI restrictions and discriminatory measures remained. This is strong negative evidence for fair competition and entrepreneurship rules.  
  IDs: `5B.4`

- **Current challenges and strategic directions for land administration system modernisation in Indonesia** — Taylor & Francis, 2024-06-06, [link](https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/14498596.2024.2360531)  
  The article says Indonesia’s land administration system still had regulatory gaps, inefficient registration, validation issues, and resource constraints. That is negative evidence on property-rights fairness: the system was improving, but not yet cleanly secure or efficient.  
  IDs: `5B.4`

- **Indonesia Growth and Jobs Report Running Faster, for Longer: Structural Transformation, Productivity, and Good Jobs** — World Bank, 2024, [link](https://www.worldbank.org/en/country/indonesia/publication/indonesia-growth-and-jobs-report-running-faster-for-longer-structural-transformation-productivity-and-good-jobs)  
  The report diagnoses market power, regulatory barriers, and non-tariff and services restrictions as key drags on competition, innovation, productivity, and job creation. This is the clearest negative evidence that fair, pro-competition rules were still incomplete in 2024.  
  IDs: `5B.4`, also `5B.1`

**Search Gap**
I did not find a 2024 source showing a sweeping competition-law overhaul, a major rollback of SOE advantages, or a decisive liberalization of product markets. The strongest evidence is mixed: real land and investment facilitation on one side, but persistent trade, entry, and competition barriers on the other.
